Continue ~63kms (paved) until you reach the single lane bridge over the Fraser River. Turn right onto the Sinclair Road, and after 0.5 km turn left onto the Pass Lake FSR. At km 46.5, turn right onto the Sande FSR and the site is located on the right side of the road at approx. 9 km.

name: East Maury Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed 20 km and turn left onto Road 9.  Find the access road to the site on the right at 6.5 km. Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Fletcher Lake
driving_directions: From Balfour, drive 23.0 KM along highway 31 towards Kaslo, and turn left onto a dirt road (4.2 KM north of the Woodbury Creek Resort).  Zero your odometer at the start of the Woodbury-Fletcher FSR.  At 1.1 KM (the crest of the hill) turn right on to Fletcher Creek Road.  At 2.8 KM take the left fork. At 3.7 KM bear right. At 7.3 Km stay left. At 11.5 go right and begin to drive though recent logging. Road is very rough from here (high clearance 4x4) with deep water bars. At 12.5 KM park at the old logging landing. From here walk a few hundred feet along an old de-activated road to find the trail head going off up to the left.

name: Kettle River
driving_directions: Drive ~30km east of Cherryville on Hwy 6, and head south on Kettle River FSR. Located on the east side of the road ~14.9 km down the Kettle River FSR.

name: Starvation Lake
driving_directions: Off of Hwy 16 turn north on Babine Lake Road travelling for 53 km then left onto the Nilkitkwa FSR. Continue until approximately 71 km. Turn right at Starvation Lake three blade sign. Continue on this road for 2 km. Radio use is recommended due to high industrial traffic in area.

name: Manson River
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, head south and turn onto the Causeway Road. Keep left at the first T just off the highway. After crossing  the bridge over Williston, keep to the right and merge with the Finlay North FSR.  The site is located at 104km on the left side of the road. The site can also be accessed from 0km of the Finlay North off Highway 97.

name: Oyama Lake
driving_directions: From Oyama: Off Middle Bench Road, turn east onto Todd Road and drive 0.7km. Then turn right onto Oyama Lake Road. Drive 9.2km and then bear right onto Oyama Lake Resort Forest Service Road. In 2.8km you will arrive at Oyama Lake.

name: Haddo Lake
driving_directions: Located approximately 36 km. (22 mi.) northeast of the town of Winfield. From the city of Kelowna travel north on Hwy. #97 to Winfield. Turn east off Hwy. #97 onto the Beaver Lake Road. Follow this road to Doreen Lake. 3 km. (2 mi.) past Doreen Lake turn south (right) and follow this road to Haddo, final access may be rough.

name: Old Fort
driving_directions: Near Granisle, off Hwy 16 take Hwy 118 through Granisle and up Topley Landing Road for about 30km, site access road is located on the right hand side and marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Woods Lake North
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 97 N and turn south onto Ingram Forest Service Road. At 7.25km, bear right and stay on Ingram FSR. At 11km, Ingram FSR becomes Jimmy FSR.  Travel up 15.7km up Jimmy FSR and then bear right onto Woods Lake Forest Service Road. It is 2.4km to the south end of the lake, but there are developed campsite facilities all along the east side of the lake to the north end.

name: Aspen
driving_directions: Near Houston off Hwy 16 turn onto Morice River FSR, site is located at 17.5 km on Morice River FSR and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Italia Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed 15 km and find the site on the left.  Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Inga Lake
driving_directions:
From Fort St John along the Alaska Highway drive 70 km north to the Inga Lake PDR.   Recreation Site signs are along the Alaska Hwy.  The site is 2 km off the Alaska Hwy
**This is an active Service Road. Use caution when entering the Recreation Site.**

name: Bisson Lake
driving_directions: Go east of Cherryville and travel 2.5 km south on the Kettle River Forest Service Road. Turn north onto KettleBison FSR and travel 2.4 km and take the left fork onto Bison FSR. This last 2.3 km stretch of road is extremely eroded and nearly impassable. 4WD is required beyond this fork.

name: Gates Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~75kms north of Prince George - Just past the Bear Lake Community take the first left onto the Davie Muskeg (200) FSR. Turn left at 277km onto the 8600 Road. The site is located on the left side of the road after a few km's at 8679km.

name: The Grotto
driving_directions: Approximately 27 km south of Atlin on Warm Bay Road.  (Warm Bay Recreation Site at 24km, natural warm springs at ~25km).

name: Stony Lake West
driving_directions: From Highway 97, turn onto the Naver Creek (700) Road at Dunkley Mill. Follow this road for approximately 58km and turn left onto the Willow-Stony Road. Follow this road and keep to the right when you reach a junction. Proceed along this road and this will be the first rec site you reach along the right side of the road.

name: Browne Lake
driving_directions: From the city of Kelowna travel southeast on Hwy. #33 to the Hydraulic (McCulloch Reservoir) Lake Road. Turn west (right) and follow this road 2 km. (1.2 mi.) past Hydraulic Lake. Turn north (right) on a secondary road (Brown FSR) and follow it to Browne Lake. Browne is approximately 46 km. (29 mi.) southeast of Kelowna.

name: Stukemapten Lake
driving_directions: From Vavenby take Vavenby/Adams FSR to 38km. Turn right onto Adams West FSR. Drive for 9kms and turn left onto Road 40 (Adams East FSR). Drive for 14.5kms and turn left onto Momich FSR. Drive for 21kms and turn right onto Celesta Creek FSR. Drive for 1.1km to Rec Site on right.

name: Baird Lake
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 97 to Lumby to Mabel Lake Road to Trinity Valley Road to Hidden Lake Forest Service Road. At km 13.5 up Hidden Lake Forest Service Road, take the right access road onto Baird-Hidden Forest Service Road, and travel an additional 2 km to Baird Lake. The road splits and there are two campsites on either end of the lake.

name: Old Man Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~75kms north of Prince George - Just past the Bear Lake Community take the first left onto the Davie Muskeg (200) FSR. Turn left at 280km on to the 8700 Road.  Site is located at 8785.6km.

name: Punchaw Lake
driving_directions: Travel west of Prince George and turn left on to the Blackwater Rd - proceed 27kms until you reach Baldy Hughes community.  The highway turns to gravel and begins at 0km.  The site is located at 24km. The final stretch of road into the site may be rough and subject to seasonal water issues; please drive with caution as you enter the site.

name: Lawrence Lake West
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed 13.5 km and find the site on the left.  Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Bonney Lake
driving_directions:
Access to this site is indicated at the Orenda Forest Service Road off of Hwy. 37. To access the Orenda Forest Service Road you must turn into the Elsworth camp (approx. 136 km north of Kitwanga) and drive through until you see a brown Recreation Site sign. It is approximately 34km to Bonney Lake along the Orenda Forest Service road. It is passable by two-wheel drive vehicles but it is recommended to take a vehicle with good clearance. This route is in better condition than the Brown Bear Forest Service Road route as of Summer 2021.  

A second access to this site is indicated by the Recreation Site sign, off the east side of Hwy 37, (approx. 110 km north of Kitwanga).  It is approximately 35 km to Bonney Lake along the Brown Bear Forest Service Road from Hwy. 37.  The road is passable by two wheel drive vehicles, but it is recommended that the vehicles have good clearance.  At approx. 25 km the Brown Bear F.S. Road is intersected by the Orenda Mainline Road, keep to the right.  At the intersection of the Kwinageese road, at approximately 32 km. keep left.  You are now back on the Brown Bear F.S. Road which leads to Bonney Lake.

name: Government Lake
driving_directions: Access directly to the site is by 4WD vehicle, ATV or foot only.

name: Sicily Lake South
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed 11 km and find the site on the left. Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Hidden Lake
driving_directions: Accessed off Trinity Valley Road, 13 km up Hidden Lake Road

name: Stony Lake
driving_directions: From Tumbler Ridge drive south on Hwy 52 E for 54 km. Watch for highway signs indicating the turn-off on to the Stony Lake Access Road. The turn-off will be on your right hand side. It is a short 1.6 km drive to reach the recreation site from the highway.

name: Dennis Lake
driving_directions: From Avola on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn north onto Avola West Frontage Rd, then north again onto Messiter Station Rd for 2km.  Turn left onto Avola Mtn FSR and continue for 12km, then turn left onto Mad River FSR for 1.5 km. (Last section is brushy).  Rec site is on the right.

name: Fishhook Lake
driving_directions:
Drive approximately 85 Km on highway 97 North and turn right on Chuchinka Red Rocky/Colbourne (2000) FSR. Keep left at the first main junction, and the site is at 832km.  There is alternate access through the 700/800 Rd (south of Bear Lake - Winton Global Mill access road).

Please note that this area is extremely busy with industrial traffic. The use of 2-way radios is highly recommended. Please drive cautiously at all times and be aware of high volumes of heavy industrial traffic.

name: Foot Lake
driving_directions: From Dawson Creek, drive south on Hwy 2 for 30 km to Hwy 52.  Drive 38 km south on Hwy 52, then turn right (West) onto the Noel Resource Road. Drive 16 km on the Noel Rd to Foot Lake (Boot). There is a Recreation Site Sign on Hwy 52.

name: Grizzly Lake East
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 5km, then turn right onto Road 5. Continue for 15 km and find the site on the left.

name: Borrow Pit 8
driving_directions: THE SITE IS LOCATED AT 416KM ON THE ALASKA HWY

name: Telkwa River
driving_directions: From Highway 16 in Telkwa, turn onto Hankin Ave which turns into Riverside Street as you cross the bridge over the Bulkley River. Stay on the same road and it turns into Telkwa Coalmine Rd. Stay right on Telkwa Coalmine road until you see the turn for Telkwa River FSR on your left, proceed up Telkwa River FSR until you cross the Telkwa River, the Recreation Site access road is just past the bridge on your right.

name: James Lake
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 33 and turn North onto Goudie Road. 3.1 km after leaving highway you turn left to stay on Goudie Road for an additional 2.6 km. Then the road turns from paved to gravel surface at James Lake Forest Service Road. Take the left hand fork after you drive a further 0.9 km. Drive another 7.2 km to the Recreation Site, which will be on the right hand side of the road. This is a rough road and there are limited turnaround spots in the campground.

name: Trout Lake
driving_directions: Head East from Southbank, following Uncha Lake Road for 11.8 km. Turn right onto the Campbell road for 4.7 km, turning left onto the Binta Road. Follow Binta Road 10.4 km until the 4-way, then continue East on the Binta North FSR for ~14.6 km. Turn Left and head east for 9.8 km along road (unknown name).

name: Twinkle Lake
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 near Houston, turn onto Morice River FSR, proceed about 40km down Morice River FSR (driving past Aspen and Owen Lake Recreation Sites amongst others), the FSR turns to Morice Owen FSR, then turn right onto Morice Nadina FSR at about 60km, proceed on Morice Nadina FSR for about 15km where it turns into Huckleberry Mine FSR, stay on this mainline following signs for Twinkle Lake for about 20km. Access road will be on the left and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Stony Lake East
driving_directions: From Highway 97, turn onto the Naver Creek (700) Road at Dunkley Mill. Follow this road for approximately 58km and turn left onto the Willow-Stony Road. Follow this road and keep to the right when you reach a junction. Proceed along this road and this will be the third rec site you reach along the right side of the road.

name: Okanagan Boulderfields
driving_directions: From Chute Lake Road in Kelowna Lat 119ﾰ 29' 57.50" Long,  W  49ﾰ 47' 44.19" N , turn  Southward onto Gillard FSR for +/- 8.706 Km, once at the KVR turn eastward onto the KVR  for +/- 1.858 Km and then onto an access road Northward for  +/- 0.727 Km.

name: Holstein Lake
driving_directions: Located northeast of the city of Vernon. From Vernon take Hwy. #6 east to the community of Lumby where you will turn left on Shuswap Avenue.Follow the signs for Mabel Lake Provincial Park along the Lumby-Mabel Lake Rd. Turn right on Silverhills Forest Service Road. 13.9 km from pavement turn right and drive .6 km. A rough road exits to the left which you take for 400 meters which gets you to the Rec Site.

name: Tete Jaune Spawning Grounds
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed north on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 8km and turn left onto Blackman Road.  Continue for 10km and turn left onto Old Tete Jaune Cache Rd.  Proceed 2.5km and find the site access road just across the train tracks on the right.

name: Big Sheep Ck
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 3B and 22, at the Le Roi Mine Museum in Rossland, travel 0.4 km south on Highway 22. Turn right onto the "Old Cascade Highway", across from the Rossland Motel. Follow this good 2 wheel drive gravel road up over Record Ridge and down into the Big Sheep Creek Valley. Just past the 22 km marker, the road forks. Turn left onto the Big Sheep Creek FSR. You will pass along farms and by cabins on the road. The sites is at 9.2 km on the left side.

name: Swalwell Lake
driving_directions: Located approximately 17 km. (11 mi.) Northeast of the town of Winfield (Lake Country). From the city of Kelowna travel north on Hwy. #97 to Winfield. Turn east off Hwy. #97 onto Beaver Lake Road and follow it to Swalwell (Beaver) Lake.

name: Big Lake
driving_directions: From Chetwynd BC, head North on the Don Phillips Way / Hwy 29 for 4 km. Then turn right onto Jackfish Lake Rd for 15 km, turn left to stay on Jackfish Rd for 13.5 km. Then turn left onto Howe Rd for 1km, the site will be on the left.

name: Yellowjacket Creek
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km, then turn east onto Cedarside Road towards Kinbasket Lake.  Continue onto Canoe East Forest Service Road/Canoe River Forest Rd for 18km and then turn right onto the site access road. Caution: may be industrial traffic.

name: Streak Lake
driving_directions: Drive 7km east of Vernon on Highway 6. Turn right onto King Edward Forest Service Road. At 4km, bear right to stay on King Edward FSR. At 12.6km, bear left to stay on King Edward FSR. After 1.7km, bear right, and travel an additional 1km into Streak Lake. Access is very rough, and 4wd high clearance is recommended.

name: Goat Mtn. Lake
driving_directions: From HWY 6 turn South on Park Lane (near Lavington), go 1.3 km then left on Learmouth Rd, then at the 3 km mark go left on Whitevale Rd. At 4.3km you hit gravel which is Aberdeen Main FSR. At 14.2 km there is a fork, turn left on the Goat Mtn Rd (board #14). At the the 31 km mark you will reach Goat Mtn Rec Site.

name: Emerald Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~65kms north of Prince George, turn right off of Hwy 97 (look for the "McEwan" sign). Keep to the left at the first junction and follow this main access road. The  site is at 3km. At 1.5-2kms you will pass by Crystal Lake recreation site.

name: Silence Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, proceed 5 km east and turn north onto Raft River Forest Service Road/Road 9.  Continue for 35 km and find the short 300m access road on the right.

name: Taltapin Lake
driving_directions: Near Burns Lake, head north on Babine Road for 19.5 km, until you reach the Augier FSR. Turn right onto and follow the Augier for ~10.2 km. Turn Left onto the Grizzly Road and follow for 2 km, then Turn Right onto the Taltapin Road. Follow Taltapin Road for 6.6 km to reach the site.

name: Nadina Lake
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 near Houston, turn onto Morice River FSR, proceed about 40km down Morice River FSR (driving past Aspen and Owen Lake Recreation Sites amongst others), the FSR turns to Morice Owen FSR, then turn right onto Morice Nadina FSR at about 60km, proceed on Morice Nadina FSR for about 15km then turn right onto Morice Tahtsa FSR and proceed about 10km on Morice Tahtsa, follow signs to Nadina Lake Lodge, drive past the Nadina River spawning channels to the Recreation Site.

name: Milford Lake
driving_directions: The Milford Lake road leaves the west side of Highway #31, 9.4 km north of Kaslo. Travel up Milford Lake Road for 8.0 km to a junction. Turn right at this junction and continue for another 0.8 km to the lake. 4WD High Clearance Vehicles Only.

name: Derrick Lake
driving_directions: Access to this site is indicated by the Recreation Site sign, off the east side of Hwy 37, approx. 2 km north of the Bonus Lake Rec Site (approx. 87 km north of Kitwanga).  Site access follows several km (~7) of rough forest service road large RVs not recommended.

name: Six Mile Bay
driving_directions: Travel north of Mackenzie to the Parsnip West FSR. Proceed for approx. 41km and the site is accessed via a left turn. Stay right at the first fork after turning off the Parsnip west and you will come to the site within 1 km.

name: High Lake
driving_directions: Access is either via the Oyama Lake Road or the King Edward Lake Road. This Site doesn't have any ammenities

name: Lamprey Creek
driving_directions: Approx. 43 km on Morice River FSR

name: Mitten Lake
driving_directions: Located at 24km on Helen Lake Forest Service Road.    North of the communities of Hazelton and Kispiox. Head north on Kispiox Valley Rd then at 28km turn left at Poplar Park road, go over the Kispiox River and proceed to Helen Lake FSR, take a left up Helen Lake FSR and site is located at 24km on right hand side and marked with 3 blade sign  - OR - Take Kispiox trail, proceed to 58km on Kispiox Trail, take a left over the bridge on Kispiox River and turn left on Helen Lake Forest Service Road - OR - take Mitten Main off Hwy 37 and turn right down Helen Lake road to get to the site.

name: Snowshoe Lake
driving_directions:
Access: From the Needles Rest Area at the ferry terminus, travel west on Highway 6 for 14.4 km.Just before the highway crosses Inonoaklin Creek, turn right onto a 4 wheel drive gravel road. Follow this road through the gravel pit onto a rough dirt road. After crossing a cattle guard at 1.5 km the road forks. Take the right fork, marked with a brown 4x4 post with white lettering, signed "Snowshoe Lake". Continue along this road for another 3 km to the recreation site. 

Alternate Access: From the Needles Rest Area at the ferry terminus, travel west on Highway 6 for 4.4 km. Turn right onto the "Whatshan Lake Road". At the junction with the Barnes Creek road, turn left and cross over the Whatshan River. Just past the power station, which is at the "7 km" marker on the "Barnes Creek Forest Service Road", turn left onto the "Snowshoe Lake Road", which is marked with a white and red sign, nailed to a tree. Proceed 1.4 km. Turn left onto a road marked "Branch 1". Proceed 1.5 km to just past a "10 km" yellow and black marker on the right hand side of the road. Turn right onto a narrow, dirt 2 wheel drive road that follows the power lines for 2 km to Snowshoe Lake. Note: the last 1.6 km is very steep, narrow and rutted, suitable for high clearance 2 wheel drive vehicles in dry weather.

name: MOORE (BULLMAN) LAKE Moore (Bullman) Lake
driving_directions: From Kelowna, Postill Forest Service Road, drive 13.7km and then turn left onto Bullman Creek Forest Service Road. Drive 300m and stay right, and then after another 900m, stay left. It is another 2 km to the Recreation Site.

name: Kitseguecla Lake
driving_directions: From Highway 16 turn onto Kitseguecla Loop Road and follow that for 750 meters to the left turn (over the railroad tracks) for Kitseguecla Lake Road. Follow Kitsequecla Lake Road, crossing the railroad tracks, for 13 km where you will see a signboard indicating Kitsequecla Lake and Taltzen Lake Recreation Sites. Turn right at the signboard and follow this road for approximately 3km to the site, the access road to the site is located on the left hand side of the road and you will see Kitseguecla Lake on your left while enroute to this site.

name: Coldscaur Lake South
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 northwest of Clearwater for 27km.  Sites are on the left. Use caution: active log hauling road.

name: Mcdonald Lake
driving_directions: Approx. 10km along Rufner Mine Road, north of Atlin.

name: Wapiti Crossing
driving_directions: From Dawson Creek, drive 30 km to Hwy 52/Boundry Road, drive another 97 km to the Wapiti FSR.  Drive another 25 km down the Wapiti FSR to the Recreation Site.

name: Wilson Lake W
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 6 and 23 in Nakusp, travel east on Highway 6 towards New Denver for 6.3 km. Turn left onto the "Wilson Lake Road". Take this good 2 wheel drive, gravel road up Wensley Creek, past the sawmill. Stay left at the "Wilson Lake Forest Service Road" junction. Continue straight ahead for another 700 meters to another junction. Take the right fork, down a good 2 wheel drive dirt road, for 400 meters to the Wilson Lake West Recreation Site.

name: Howser
driving_directions: From the community of Meadow Creek head north on Highway 31 for 8.3 km. After crossing over the Lardeau River, turn right at Howser Station Road. Follow this road through Howser for 2.0 km to a fork. The road to the left takes you 0.3 km to the Howser Recreation Site. The road to the right will take you 0.3 km to Glayco Beach day-use area.

name: Specs Lakes
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 6 to Aberdeen Road. Access is to the left on a short, narrow road at around 24 km on Aberdeen Road.

name: Indian Bay
driving_directions: Near Southbank (Francois Lake), from Burns Lake take Hwy 35 and Colleymount Rd to the Northbank ferry terminal, cross Francois Lake on the ferry. When you get off the ferry, take the first left off Keefes Landing Road onto Uncha Lake Rd, travel east on Uncha Lake Rd for 2.3 km, then turn left on Indian Bay Road, and travel for ~1.0 km, access road is straight off the last corner on Indian Bay Road (eg. don't turn west/left at the corner).

name: McCULLOCH RESERVOIR
driving_directions: From the city of Kelowna, travel southeast on Hwy. #33 to the Hydraulic (McCulloch Reservoir) Lake Road southeast of Kelowna to 201 Forest Service Road to McCulloch Rd. Follow the road until you see the recreation site sign. Turn left and drive over the KVR and 100m past you will be at Hydraulic and 1.2 km up the road you will be at McCulloch Lake.

name: Elizabeth Lake
driving_directions: North of the communities of Hazelton and Kispiox. Head north on Kispiox Valley Rd for 13km then turn right onto Kispiox Trail and continue past Upper Kispiox Recreation Site, at about 54km the access road will be on your right and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Augier Lake
driving_directions: In Burns Lake, head north along Babine Lake Road for 19.5km until you reach the Augier FSR, turn left on Augier FSR and follow it for about 10km, then turn right onto Donald Landing Road and follow it for about 5kms until you get to the site marked with a 3 blade sign and kiosk.

name: Wilson Lake East
driving_directions:
Access from Rosebery: Turn off Highway 6, at Rosebery, onto the "East Wilson Creek Road". This road soon turns into the "Wilson Creek Forest Service Road". Follow this good 2 wheel drive gravel road. At 5 km the road forks, stay left. At 33 km a dirt road crosses the "Wilson Creek Forest Service Road", continue on the gravel road to the left. "Wilson Lake East Recreation Site" is straight ahead, at 34 km, just before the road crosses a bridge over Fitzstubbs Creek.

Access from Nakusp: From the junction of Highway 6 and 23 in Nakusp, travel east on Highway 6 towards New Denver for 6.3 km. Turn left onto the "Wilson Lake Road". Take this good 2 wheel drive, gravel road up Wensley Creek, past the sawmill. 7 km up the road, turn right onto the "Wilson Lake Forest Service Road". Follow this rough 2 wheel drive road for 7 km, as it climbs steeply over the rocky bluffs south of Wilson Lake. Several spur roads come onto it from the right. Stay straight ahead at all of these, eventually descending to the shore of Wilson Lake. The recreation site at the end of the lake, is visible across the lake, from the last steep descent.

name: Amanita Lake
driving_directions: Travel 16.5kms east of Prince George and turn left on to the Upper Fraser Rd. Continue ~63kms (paved) until you  cross the one-lane bridge (changes to unpaved) and keep left to the Church FSR. The site is located via a left turn at approx. the 8 km mark.

name: Cleswuncut Lake
driving_directions: Travel west of Prince George and turn left onto the Blackwater Rd - proceed 27kms until you reach the Baldy Hughes community.  The highway turns to gravel and begins at 0km.  The site is located at 34km.

name: Damer Lake
driving_directions: From Vernon: Drive approximately 7km east of Vernon on Highway 6 and turn right onto King Edward Forest Service Road. At 4km, bear right to stay on King Edward FSR. Then at 12.6km, bear right onto Oyama Lake Forest Service Road. After 4.8km on Oyama Lake FSR, Damer Lake is on the left side.

name: Pack River
driving_directions: From the Mackenzie Junction, head south for about 3 km and turn onto the Finlay North (Pack) FSR. The site is located at approx. 10 km on the left side of the road, just beyond the bridge over the Pack River.

name: Sheila Lake
driving_directions: In Westwold, take Douglas Lake Road south (paved to 9 km). Drive to 24.5 km and turn right (before the cattle guard) on unnamed forest service road. Locally known as Monte-Sheila FSR. After 600 m turn right. After 1.4 km cross under power lines and turn left and drive 200m to the main camping site.

name: Morley Lake
driving_directions: Approximately 40km south of Teslin, YK -- at the BC/Yukon border on Alaska Highway 1.   This site is ~1km from the highway.

name: Lund Lake
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 in Burns Lake, take Hwy 35 south and take the ferry across Francois Lake (be sure to check schedules for Francois Lake ferry). Arrive in Southbank. Travel South from Southbank for 18.3 km on Keefe's Landing Road. At the fork, continue west down the Keefe's Landing Road for another 20.7 km. Turn right on the Ootsa Nadina Road and travel for ~23.2 km, then turn right and head 600 m north to reach the site. Can be accessed via Houston on the Morice-Owen, Owen East, Ootsa-Nadina FSR's as well.

name: Chubb Lake
driving_directions: This site is located south of Prince George off Highway 97. At ~9kms south of Hixon turn right (follow the Chubb Lake Bible camp sign). Take the next left (100m) and continue until you reach the the "Y" in the road, keep to the right. At ~7km turn right and the site is within 1km.

name: Red Sand Lake
driving_directions: From Terrace drive west along Highway 16.  200 m. west of the Kalum River turn north onto the first road (West Kalum forestry road), follow for 26 km before turning at the Recreation sites sign. Access to the site is difficult due to damage from significant flooding events, be sure to drive with caution.

name: Gordon Bay
driving_directions: Adams Lake North, km 64.

name: Jimmy Lake
driving_directions:
Follow Hwy 97N to Ingram Forest Service Road, drive 7.1 km take the right hand fork. At 11 km Ingram FSR turns into Jimmy Lake Road. At 21.9 km turn left and drive 500 meters to the Rec Site. There are two camping areas.

The access is good. Note that access through Douglas Lake Road is through private land.

name: Wolverine Lake
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, turn left onto the Causeway Road and turn left at the first T just off the highway. After crossing the bridge, keep to the right and merge with the Finlay North FSR. Proceed to approx. km 99 and turn left onto the Manson FSR. Travel for approx. 60km and the site is located on the right side of the road, across from the turn off to Manson Creek.

name: Burden Lake
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, head south to the Causeway Road. Turn left at the first T just off the highway. After crossing the bridge, merge with the Finlay North FSR at ~20km.  The entrance to the site is located at 71km on the left side of the road. This road comes to a Y fork after approx. 1 km, and both sides of the fork lead to separate portions of the rec site.

name: Six Mile Lakes
driving_directions: Travel north from Nelson on highway #3A for 8.0 km to Six Mile Lakes road. Follow Six Miles Lakes road for 10.0 km to a fork in the road. Then take the right fork for 3.0 km to the recreation site . The road is suitable for a High clearance 2wd vehicles or 4x4 vehicles , although the last 3.0 km are very rough in sections.

name: Naver Creek
driving_directions: Travel 17.5kms south of Hixon.  Turn left onto the 700rd near Dunkley Lumber.  Site is located just past the "Y" intersection (to the left) at 718km.

name: Teapot Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17.5kms south of Hixon, turn left on to the 700rd near Dunkley Lumber.  Turn left at ~751km.  The site is located 5.5kms in at the end of the Teapot Lake road (keep left at the first junction).

name: St. Marie Lake (East)
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George (Hwy 97).  Turn left onto the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km). Turn right at 121km (T-junction). Proceed to km 139 and the site will be accessed by a right hand turn at this point. The site is about 300 metres in from the Willow-Cale FSR.

name: Taite Creek
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 6 and "Applegrove Road" in Fauquier, travel south on "Applegrove Road" for 9.6 km on a good, 2 wheel drive, gravel road. 100 meters before the bridge over Taite Creek, turn right onto a dirt road. Follow this narrow, 2 wheel drive road for 1 km to the recreation site on the lake shore.

name: Pratt Lake
driving_directions: Take Hwy 97, just North of Monte Lake turn onto Mill Road.  Drive approximately 3km and then turn right onto Monte-George FSR. Drive 8.4km and stay right on the Monte-George, and then travel another 7.7km and stay left (straight) on the Monte-George. Drive 2.3km and stay right on the Monte-George. Drive another 1.3km, and stay right on the Monte-George. Drive another 4.3km and stay right on the Monte-George. Drive another 1.8km and stay left on the Monte-George. Drive another 2.4km and there are two accesses to the lake on the west side of the road.

name: Hydraulic Lake
driving_directions: From the city of Kelowna, travel southeast on Hwy. #33 to the Hydraulic (McCulloch Reservoir) Lake Road. Turn west (right) and follow this road a few kilometers to the lake. Hydraulic is approximately 35 km. (22 mi.) southeast of Kelowna.

name: Nicklen Lake West
driving_directions: From Lavington, travel Aberdeen FSR to 10.75km marker, and turn left onto Haddo FSR. After 3.2km, at the 14 km marker on Haddo FSR, keep left onto Goat FSR. Nicklen Lake East is another 8.6km at km marker 22km on Goat FSR.

name: Reflector Lake East
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 5km, then turn right onto Road 5. Continue for 12 km and find the site on the left. CAUTION: Road 5 very rough

name: Cottonwood Beach
driving_directions: Access via Lumby: head north on Mabel Lake FSR and at marker Km 27 on Mabel Lake FSR, turn west head toward lake, 3 km down to the campsite.

name: Butternut Lake
driving_directions: From the Mackenzie Junction, head south for about 3 km and turn onto the Finlay North (Pack) FSR. At about 10 km, turn left onto the Sabai Mainline, just past the bridge over the Pack River. Proceed for an additional 10 km and turn left onto the Butternut FSR. The site is located about 3 km along this road (keep left at the main Y just after the bridge over the small creek).

name: Postill Lake
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 97 to Postil Lake Road, travel 15.8 km directly into site.

name: Surprise Lake
driving_directions: Approximately 20km east of Atlin on Surprise Lake Road.

name: Maxan Lake
driving_directions: From Burns Lake, travel east for 15 km on Hwy 16 to the turnoff for Decker Lake Sawmill. Follow this road for approx. 2.5 km to the start of Maxan Road. At 6 km on the Maxan, turn right onto the Thompson road, following the Thompson until the 17 km sign board. Cross the bridge and turn left onto the Maxan Creek FSR, drive ~1.5 km south, turning left at the junction. Head north 650 meters then turn right onto the next road follow for 1.7 km to reach the site. Alternate access is Forestdale Road from Hwy 16 between Rose Lake and Topley.

name: Bannock Point
driving_directions:
Road Access: From the bridge on Highway 6, in Silverton, travel south along the highway for 4.5 km. Turn right off the highway at the "Bannock Point Trail" sign. It is about 3/4 km from the highway to the parking. Follow the road to the gravel pit. When the road reaches the gravel pit and opens up, continue straight, there will be gated access to the gravel work area of either side. The road then narrows and leads a short distance through the trees before opening up to the parking lot for Bannock Point. You will see an information kiosk and designated parking spots.

Boat Access: From Silverton's public boat ramp, travel south along the east shore of Slocan Lake for about 4 km. Look for a sheltered bay and the "Bannock Point Recreation Site" sign on the beach.

name: Erie Creek
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 3B and 3/6 in Salmo, travel 3.6 km west towards Trail, on Highway 3. Just before a small bridge over Erie Creek, turn right onto the "Second Relief Road". This road is paved for the first 200 meters, then turns into a good 2 wheel drive gravel road. Within 1 km you will see the "Erie Creek Forest Service Road" sign. Continue up this road. The road forks at 7 km, stay straight ahead (to the left). The road forks again at 8.5 km, again stay left, descending into the valley. Cross over the bridge, at 10 km. The recreation site is on your right.

name: Salmon Run
driving_directions: Located east of Terrace, approx. 30 km on the Copper River FSR. The Copper FSR is open but due to flooding damage in Fall 2024 there is a short section of road the requires a high clearance 4x4 vehicle.

name: Griffin Sawmill Recreation Site
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km, then turn east onto Cedarside Road towards Kinbasket Lake.  Continue onto Canoe East Forest Service Road/Canoe River Forest Rd for 20km and then turn right into the site.  Caution: may be industrial traffic.

name: Philip Lakes
driving_directions: Travel  ~11kms south from Mackenzie and turn right on to the Causeway (then turn left). After crossing the bridge over Williston Lake keep to the left and continue straight through the main junction (Finlay North FSR (18km)& Finlay-Philip). The site is located at ~53km on the Finlay-Philip FSR. (You can also enter from the Finlay North FSR off hwy97 instead of the Causeway).

name: Nugget Lake
driving_directions: Access is off Jimmy Lake Road; at the end of the logged area follow a very rough 4WD trail for 2km to the lake.

name: Bairnsfather Creek
driving_directions: Follow Babine Lake Road for approx. 51 km to the start of / turnoff for the Nilkitkwa (4000 Road) FSR. Follow the Nilkitkwa FSR to the 53-54 km board and turn onto the 454 Road, where you will find the recreation site (campground) less than 1 km down the road.

name: Muskwa River Boat Launch
driving_directions: From Fort Nelson drive north on the Alaska Highway (Hwy 97) for 45 minutes. Turn left on to the Kledo Forest Service Road.  Drive to the end of the road to reach the campground and boat launch.

name: Hart Farm
driving_directions: From Terrace drive west along Highway 16.  200 m. west of the Kalum River turn north onto the first road (West Kalum forestry road) for 26 km.

name: Horse Creek Recreation Site
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km, then turn east onto Cedarside Road towards Kinbasket Lake.  Continue onto Canoe East Forest Service Road/Canoe River Forest Rd for 20.5km and then turn right onto the short site access road. Caution: may be industrial traffic.

name: Bruer Creek
driving_directions: Drive ~30km east of Cherryville on Hwy 6, and head south on Kettle River FSR. Located on the west side of the road ~14.5 km down the Kettle River FSR.

name: Catherine Lake
driving_directions: Access from Arrow Park Ferry: At the ferry terminus set your odometer. Your odometer readings will not conform to the km signs on the road. Within 200 meters of leaving the ferry, turn right onto the road marked "Saddle Mountain Road Revelstoke". Follow this road, past the "Saddle Lookout" road, for 11.6 km to the junction with the "Low Pass Road". Reset your odometer. Stay right following the lake on the "Blackie Rogers Road" for another 12.9 km to a major intersection marked "Fostall Point", "Fostall Road", "Blackie Road" and "Cameron Lake Road". Continue straight ahead on the "Fostall Road". Reset your odometer. Travel 5.2 km up the "Fostall Road" to a junction with "North Fostall Revelstoke". Turn right onto the "North Fostall Revelstoke" road. Reset your odometer. Continue along this road for 3.6 km. At the junction with "Middle Fostall Road", stay right on "North Fostall Revelstoke".Travel another 2 km to a junction with "Vanstone Road". Turn right onto "Vanstone Road" and proceed 4.2 km to the "17 km" road marker. Turn right onto a narrow, dirt, 2 wheel drive road. Travel 1.7 km to the Catherine Lake Recreation Site.

name: Honeymoon Bay
driving_directions: Adams Lake West FSR km 47.5. Site can be approached from south or north.

name: Narrow Lake East
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George (Hwy 97).  Turn left onto the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km). Turn right at 121km (T-junction), turn left at ~171km and the site is located at ~11km on the Willow-Narrow FSR. Please note the final access road is very rough for approximately 200 metres - it is 4WD accessible for a high clearance vehicle only. Towing large trailers is not recommended at this site.

name: Halfway-Graham
driving_directions: From Fort St John, head north to the Upper Halfway Road.  Turn west and drive for 50 km to the site.

name: Ideal Lake
driving_directions: From the city of Kelowna travel east on Hwy 33. From Philpot Road, travel 20.6km. Turn left at the Ideal/Philpot FSR junction and travel another 1.3km to the recreation site. From Lavington, at the end of Whitevale Road, travel up Aberdeen Forest Service Road. Go 33.2km up Aberdeen FSR, and then turn left onto Ideal/Philpott FSR. Travel an additional 1.3km to the recreation site.

name: Garland Bay
driving_directions: From the community of Riondel on the east shore of Kootenay Lake, take a right turn on to Eastman Avenue and proceed to Tam O'Shanter Creek. Take the Kootenay Lake East forest service road 9.0 km to the Bernard forest service road junction, then take the left fork for 4.0 km to the site. The road is suitable for 2wd vehicles.

name: Sweeney Lake E
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 near Houston, turn onto Morice River FSR, proceed about 40km down Morice River FSR (driving past Aspen and Owen Lake Recreation Sites amongst others), the FSR turns to Morice Owen FSR, then turn right onto Morice Nadina FSR at about 60km, proceed on Morice Nadina FSR for about 15km where it turns into Huckleberry Mine FSR, keep right on this mainline following signs for Twinkle Lake for about 37km then turn right onto the Sweeney Lake access road, proceed for about 7km to get to Sweeney Lake East site (just beyond is Sweeney lake West). Access is on the left side of the road and site is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Evely
driving_directions: Located on Westside Road north of Fintry Provincial Park - approximately 34 km north of Kelowna or 49 km south of Vernon.

name: Tudyah Lake
driving_directions: From the Mackenzie Junction, head south for about 3km and turn onto the Finlay North (Pack) FSR. The site is located via a left turn at about the 3 km mark. The site is another 1 km past this turn off and offers easy 2WD access.

name: Sugar Creek
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 6 to Cherryville turn onto Sugar Lake Road and turn onto Kate Creek FSR. Set odometer to 0.  At 2km cross over Outlet Creek Bridge. At 2.6km stay left. At 3.6km stay left at Vidler Rd. At 11.4km cross over Sitcom River Bridge. Road is narrow from here, go slow and be cautious of oncoming traffic.  At 14.4km stay right. At 14.7km take lower left fork road (Weyco Transfer). At 16.7km turn left at Sugar Creek Recreation Site before bridge. At 17.3km, you have arrived at the Host Site.

name: Twin Bays Site
driving_directions: From Kaslo BC Head North on Highway 31 for approximately 35 KM. just before Cooper Creek Turn right on Argenta Road.(you will see sign for Jumbo/Monica hiking trails just before the road). Procced straight and cross a bridge over the River, follow the Duncan Lake FSR main line (do not turn right to Argenta) for 14.5 KM to find the Twin bays Recreation Site.

name: Flyfish Lake #2
driving_directions: From Winfield. Turn east on the Beaver Lake Road and follow it to 19.2km up the Dee Lake Forest Service Road. Turn right onto an unnamed and unmaintained access road. Drive the 1km on rough 4WD only to access Loon Lake.

name: Doreen Lake
driving_directions: From Winfield Hwy 97, turn east onto Beaver Lake Road. The paved portion of the road is usually poor, but the gravel portions are normally well maintained. Drive 15 km, and at Beaver Lake Resort, turn left onto Dee Forest Service Road. Travel an additional 15 km to Doreen which will be located on the left (north) side of the road.

name: Pinaus Lake North
driving_directions:
Off Hwy 97, south of Westwold, head south on Ingram Creek FSR. At km 7.2, turn left onto Will Lake FSR. At km 8.8, stay left. At km 13, turn right onto Pinaus Lake FSR. Pinaus Lake Recreation Site is 18.1 km from Hwy 97.

There is also access east of Falkland off Hwy 97, head south on Cedar Hill Road for 3.5 km. Then bear left onto Square Lake Road and after 1.1 km, the road becomes a unpaved Forest Service Road. Drive 4.8 km on the Square-Pinaus FSR, and then bear right onto the Pinaus FSR for another 4 km and the Recreation Site access is on the left.

name: Suskwa River
driving_directions: From Smithers, follow hwy 16 west for approx. 58 km to the turn off for the Suskwa FSR. Follow the FSR for approx. 15 km where you will cross the Suskwa River, and turn left on the ILTZUL-WEST FSR. At approx. 2 km you will find the recreation site.

name: Colleymount
driving_directions: From Burns Lake, head south on Hwy 35 towards Francois Lake, then turn right onto Colleymount Road, drive past Northside ferry landing (at Francois Lake, 20min south of Burns Lake Village) and keep heading west for 27.7 km along Colleymount Road (you will drive past several other Recreation Sites along Colleymount Road enroute to this site).

name: Little Bouleau Lake
driving_directions: Hwy 97 (Westwold), turn onto Douglas Lake Rd. Travel 25.9 km (mile marker 27). Turn left onto Salmon River Road. After 6.3 km (mile marker 33), turn left to remain on Salmon River road. After 8.4 km, bear left onto Whiteman-Granite FSR. Travel 12.7 km and Little Bouleau Lake Recreation Site is on the left side of the road. Caution: there are sections of this road effected by 2021 fire, so obstacles like windfall and rocks are common. Go prepared for obstacles.

name: Palmer Lake
driving_directions: Approximately 18km south of Atlin, along Warm Bay Road.

name: Opatcho Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George. Turn left on to the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km) and turn right at the T-Junction (121km).  At 140.5km turn left on to the Opatcho lake road and drive in ~2.5kms. Turn on to the small access road, slightly to your left, which will lead in to the site.

name: Nicklen Lake East
driving_directions: From Lavington, travel Aberdeen FSR to 10.75 km marker, and turn left onto Haddo FSR. After 3.2km, at the 14 km marker on Haddo FSR, keep left onto Goat FSR. Nicklen Lake East is another 10.1km at 23.5km on Goat FSR.

name: Meadow Lake
driving_directions: Travel west of Prince George - turn left on to the Blackwater Rd - proceed 21kms and then turn right on to the Pelican FSR.  Turn left at 56km on to the '56' Road.  The site is located at 5km on the right side of the road.

name: Mud Lake
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 3 and 3B at Nancy Greene Lake Provincial Park, travel west along Highway 3 for 5.2 km.  Turn left off of the highway and follow the gravel road for 0.4 km to the recreation site.

name: Owen Lake
driving_directions: Near Houston, from Hwy 16 turn onto Morice River FSR and proceed for approximately 39 km. Site access road is on the right hand side of the Morice Owen FSR (Morice River FSR changes to Morice Owen FSR at about 29km) and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Morin Lake
driving_directions: Located at the 14.5km on the Upper Fulton Road, past Chapman Lake Recreation Site.  From Highway 16, turn onto Babine Lake Road, at 38km turn left onto Upper Fulton FSR, then travel 14.5km on Upper Fulton to get to the Rec Site. The site entrance is on the left hand side of the road.

name: Bonus Lake
driving_directions: Located approximately 5 km north of Cranberry Junction (approx. 85 km north of Kitwanga), access to the site is from the west side of the highway, where the site is just off the highway.

name: Double Lakes
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road.  Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed to 8.5 km and find the site on the left.  Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Youngs Lake
driving_directions: Travel approx. 12kms along Chief Lake road before taking a right turn along Chief Lake road, before it becomes Ness Lake Road. Travel another 12kms along Chief Lake road through the Nukko Lake community until you reach Teardrop Forest Road on the right. Approx 15kms until you take a left onto W. Creek Road. Continue along W. Creek road for another 15kms keeping to the right at both the 300 and 400 road junctions

name: Square Lake
driving_directions: Leaving HWY 97, access is via Pinaus Lake, Ingram Creek, Cedar Hills and Six Mile Roads.

name: Sock Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then turn right onto Road 1/Sock Lake Road.  Continue for 16.5 km and turn right onto a 1.3 km access road to the site.

name: Sugar Lake 1 Mile
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 6 to Cherryville turn onto Sugar Lake road. Crossing the bridge, travel 1 km up Sugar Lake FSR. At 1 km turn right onto Sugarcampsite FSR and 0.3km along the road, turn right. There is a closed gate, and access is only granted from the site operator at Sugar Lake 2 Mile.

name: Enso
driving_directions: From the Kitimat Service Centre head north along Enterprise Avenue until you reach the Wedeene Mainline Forestry Road.  Continue north along the mainline for approximately 14.5 km.

name: Mosquito Lake
driving_directions: Access from Arrow Park Ferry: At the ferry terminus set your odometer. Your odometer readings will not conform to the km signs on the road. From the ferry terminus travel straight ahead on the "Lower Mosquito Road". Continue up this road for 6 km. Just after crossing the bridge over Arrow Park (Mosquito) Creek, turn right onto the "Branch 20" road. Follow this road for 3 km. At the junction with the "West Mosquito Road" continue straight ahead. Reset your odometer. Travel north on the "West Mosquito Road" for 11.6 km, to the "27 km" road marker and the junction of the "West Mosquito Road" with the "Caribou Pass Road" and the "Fostall Road". Reset your odometer. Continue straight ahead on the "Fostall Road" for 8.9 km. Between the "19 km" and "20 km" road markers, at the junction with "Plant Road", turn left. Travel 800 meters to the recreation site.

name: BINTA LAKE South
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 in Burns Lake, take Hwy 35 south and take the ferry across Francois Lake (be sure to check schedules for Francois Lake ferry). Arrive in Southbank and take the first left off Keefes Landing Road onto Uncha Lake Road. Follow Uncha Lake Road for 11.8 km. Turn right onto the Campbell road for 4.7 km, turn left onto Binta Road. Follow Binta Road east for ~10.4 km. At the 4-way junction, travel south for 22.0 km on the Binta South FSR, turning left onto Mooney Road when you reach it. Proceed ~0.8 km along the Mooney to reach the site.

name: Howser Cr Canyon
driving_directions: From Kaslo BC Head North on Highway 31 for approximately 35 KM. just before Cooper Creek Turn right on Argenta Road.(you will see sign for Jumbo/Monica hiking trails just before the road). Procced straight and cross a bridge over the River, follow the Duncan Lake FSR main line (do not turn right to Argenta) for 34 KM to find the Howser Creek Canyon Recreation Site.

name: Mystery Lake
driving_directions: From Blue River Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Blueberry Rd.  Travel 500m and stay left, continuing onto the North Blue Forest Service Road for 10 km. Turn left onto the tight access road and proceed 400m to site.

name: Ahbau Lake
driving_directions: The turn off is located approximately 17.5 km south of Hixon on Highway 97. Turn left onto the Naver Creek (700) Road at Dunkley Lumber Mill. Drive for approximately 35 km and turn right at KM 735. Drive for approximately 2.5 km, and the site is a right turn around KM 1038. The site is easily accessible by 2WD vehicles.

name: Kimta Creek
driving_directions: Travel north (NW) of Mackenzie on the Parsnip West FSR. The site is located at ~50.5kms on the right hand side of the Parsnip West FSR.

name: Winnifred Creek
driving_directions: This site is located along the Kettle River Main FSR 20 km south of Hwy 6.

name: COOKE CREEK
driving_directions: Take Hwy 97 to Enderby and follow signs for Mabel Lake. Drive to Ashton Creek then take Enderby-Mabel Lake Road to Cooke Creek Forest Service Road and turn right into the Recreation Site. The Cooke Creek FSR is approximately 25.8 km from HWY 97.

name: Windy Point Lake
driving_directions: From the Mackenzie Junction, head south for about 3km and turn onto the Finlay North (Pack) FSR. After about 750 metres, turn right at the site entrance sign. The site is located a further 2 km along this road. Please note that the road is fairly rough and brushy. There is easy 2WD access, but vehicles with fresh paint jobs may want to assess before accessing this road.

name: Lakelse River
driving_directions: From Terrace turn left at the 4 way stop at the junction of Highways 16 and 37 and go toward the old bridge, turning left again just before the old bridge, onto Queensway Drive.  From Queensway Dr turn right onto Old Remo Road and continue for approx. 8 km.  Turn left onto the Whitebottom logging road for 5 km. until you reach the Lakelse River Rec site just before the Lakelse River bridge.

name: Upper Canoe
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km and turn west onto Cranberry Lake Rd.  Continue south for 1.1km and then turn left onto Upper Canoe Rd.  Proceed 6km and find the site on the left.

name: Morice Mtn Nordic Ski Club Trails
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 near Houston, take Buckflats Road and proceed about 7.5 km to the site, where you will see the lodge and parking area.

name: Keynton Lake
driving_directions:
~16.5km on Kitwanga Backroad from Hwy 37 in Kitwanga.    Turn left on Burdick Road (for ~1.5km) -keep right 1.5km to Keynton Lake.

NOTE:  Access from Hazelton/Kispiox side is closed indefinitely.

name: Curve Lake
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, travel south and turn onto the Causeway Road and turn left at the first T just off the highway. After crossing the bridge over Williston, keep to the right and merge with the Finlay North FSR at ~20km.  The site is located at ~112km. (The site can also be accessed from 0km of the Finlay North off Highway 97).

name: Wapiti River
driving_directions: From Dawson Creek drive 30 km to Hwy 52/Boundry Road, drive another 97 km to the Wapiti FSR.  Drive another 25 km down the Wapiti FSR to the Rec Site.

name: Clarkston Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~75kms north of Prince George - Just past the Bear Lake Community take the first left onto the Davie Muskeg (200) Road.  Turn left at 280km on to the 8700 Road.  The site is located at 8783km.

name: Binta Lake North
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 in Burns Lake, take Hwy 35 south and take the ferry across Francois Lake (be sure to check schedules for Francois Lake ferry). Arrive in Southbank and take the first left off Keefes Landing Road onto Uncha Lake Road. Head East from Southbank, following Uncha Lake Road for 11.8 km. Turn right onto Campbell road for 4.7 km, turning left onto the Binta Road. Travel east on Binta Road for 7.9 km to reach the site.

name: Ispah Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George (Hwy 97).  Turn left on to the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km).   Turn right at 121km (T-Junction). The site is located at 153.1km.

name: Fisher Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~75kms north of Prince George - Just past the Bear Lake Community take the first left onto the Davie Muskeg (200) FSR. The site is located at 222km on the left side of the road.

name: Francis Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George (Hwy 97) and turn left on to the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km).  Turn right at the T-junction at 121km. The site is a left hand turn at 134km on the Willow Cale FSR.

name: Little Wilson Lake
driving_directions: Turn off Highway 6, at Rosebery, onto the "East Wilson Creek Road". This road soon turns into the "Wilson Creek Forest Service Road". Follow this good 2 wheel drive gravel road. At 5 km the road forks, stay left. Just before the orange and white 31 km marker look for a 4x4 post on your left, painted brown with white lettering, signed "Little Wilson Lake". Turn left here, onto a rough 2 wheel drive dirt road. Follow this road for 800 meters to the campsite.

name: Mackenzie Lakes
driving_directions: Travel west of PG to the Blackwater road and proceed 27kms until you reach Baldy Hughs community.  The highway turns to gravel and begins at 0km. Mackenzie Lake West is located off the Blackwater Road via a left turn at KM 9. Mackenzie Lake East is accessed via the Lookout FSR via a left turn at KM 6.5. Follow this road for about 3 km and turn right. Follow this road for another few kilometres until your reach the site.

name: Noralee West
driving_directions: Near Burns Lake, from Hwy 16 drive south on Hwy 35 for ~22 km to the tee-junction with Colleymount Road. Turn right on Colleymount and travel west for  ~50.9 km to the site. Site is on the lakeshore on your left and marked with a 3 blade sign. Site is about 59km from Northbank (Francois Lake) ferry terminal, Colleymount road is paved until 30km and gravel after that.

name: Cut Thumb Bay
driving_directions: Travel north of Mackenzie to the Parsnip West FSR. Proceed for 33km an turn left. Follow this road for approx. 3.5 km until you reach the site.

name: Tanglechain Lake
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 turn onto Babine Lake Road.  Travel past the Upper Fulton FSR for 10.5 km. Tanglechain Recreation Site is on Babine Lake Road on the right hand side at about 48.5 km mark.  Do not turn onto Tanglechain FSR (7 kms prior to the recreation site), site access road is right off Babine Lake Road and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Sugar Lake 3 Mile
driving_directions: Follow Hwy 6 to Cherryville turn onto Sugar lake road. At km 7 of Sugar Lake FSR, turn right onto Sugarcampsite FSR and 2.25 km to access several campsites on the lake.

name: Merton Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~75kms north of Prince George - Just past the Bear Lake Community take the first left (200rd).  The site is located at 233km.

name: Mt Abriel
driving_directions: From the town of Nakusp Drive approximately 8KM North on HWY 23, the turnoff to the campsite is on the left, there are highwy signs in place 300 Meters before the turnoff. A short drive down Turner Road will lead you right into the campsite.

name: Ejas Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, turn west onto Old North Thompson Highway Road. Turn north onto Camp Two Road for 1.4 km, then take TFL 18 Road 2 out of Clearwater. Proceed 29.5  km, then turn right onto Road 20. Proceed 20 km and turn left onto Road 9.  Find the access road to the site on the right before 1 km. Use caution: Road 2 is an active log hauling road.

name: Bear Lake
driving_directions: At approximately 9 km off King Edward FSR, turn left onto Bear Lake FSR. It is an additional 3 km to Bear Lake Recreation Site, with the last 2 km being in extremely rough condition.

name: Genevieve Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17.5kms south of Hixon, turn left onto the 700rd (near Dunkley Lumber Mill).  At 712km turn right onto the 1200 Road and turn right again at 1222km to access the site. Access can be rough into the site.  The site may also be accessible 25.5kms south of Hixon (left off the highway). The site is located 13kms in (rough access?).

name: Cameron Lake
driving_directions:
Access from Arrow Park Ferry: At the ferry terminus set your odometer. Your odometer readings will not conform to the km signs on the road. Within 200 meters of leaving the ferry, turn right onto the road marked "Saddle Mountain Road Revelstoke". Follow this road, past the "Saddle Lookout" road, for 11.6 km to the junction with the "Low Pass Road". Reset your odometer. Stay right following the lake on the "Blackie Rogers Road" for another 12.9 km to a major intersection marked "Fostall Point", "Fostall Road", "Blackie Road" and "Cameron Lake Road". Turn left onto the "Cameron Lake Road". Reset your odometer. Stay on the "Cameron Lake Road" for 6.2 km, passing "Branch 10" and other new roads. At 6.2 km the road forks again. This time take the right fork. The lake will be visible soon, as the recreation site is 1.8 km from this last junction.

Alternate access from the Fostall Road: Cameron Lake can also be accessed from near the "17 km" sign on the "Fostall Road". From the "Fostall Road" to Cameron Lake it is 5.1 km. This road has some steep, rough sections. A 4x4 vehicle with good clearance is recommended.

name: Sweetin River
driving_directions: Located at 74km on Kispiox Valley Trail, north of Hazelton and Kispiox Village. Head north on Kispiox Valley Rd for 13km then turn right onto Kispiox Trail, continue past Upper Kispiox Recreation Site and Elizabeth Lake Recreation Site. At 74km the site is on the left hand side and marked with a First Nations carved totem archway and 3 blade sign.

name: Clements Lake
driving_directions: Drive North from Stewart along Highway 37A for approximately 13 km. (8 miles).  After crossing the Bitter Creek bridge take the first right.  Turn left at the first junction and follow the road, keeping to the right for another km. (.6 miles)

name: Uslika Lake
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, head south on Highway 39 and turn onto the Causeway Road (turn left at the fork just after leaving the highway). After crossing the bridge over Williston, keep to the right and merge with the Finlay North FSR. At ~175km on the Finlay North take the Finlay-Osilinka (47km section) which connects to the Thutade FSR (turn/keep left). The site is located a further 11kms.

name: Richy
driving_directions:
Access from the Needles Ferry: Zero your odometer at the Needles ferry landing on the Edgewood side. At 3.2 KM turn right off the highway on to Whatshan Lake Road. At 4.7 KM turn right on to Whatshan Forest Service Road. At 5.6 KM find a junction, stay on the main line. At 18.5 Proceed Left and stay on the Whatshan FSR. At 26.8 KM proceed left at the junction staying on the Whatshan FSR. At 27 KM Find the Richy Recreation Site on the left.


  Directions from Arrow Park Ferry: When leaving the ferry stay left onto: Stevens Road to Needles. At 8.9 Km take the left fork sign: To Needles/ Old Arrow Park . At 11.5 Km take the right fork sign: Whatshan Lake Richy/ Stevens. AT 23.2 Km Stay right onto Branch 1 Stevens. At 24.7 Km hairpin left onto Whatshan Rd. going South.  At 26.1 Km Stevens Campground on Right.  At 28.3 Km Richy Campground on Right.

name: Pine Lake (2 Sites)
driving_directions: From Terrace drive west along Highway 16.  200 m. West of the Kalum River turn North onto the first road (West Kalum forestry road).  At 11.3 km. turn left and follow along road for approx. 800 m. where a short road leads to the right and to the trail.

name: Haggkvist Lake
driving_directions: Located northeast of the city of Vernon. From Vernon take Hwy. #6 east to the community of Lumby where you will turn left on Shuswap Avenue. Follow the signs for Mabel Lake Provincial Park along the Lumby-Mabel Lake Rd. Turn right on Silverhills Forest Service Road. After 23.6 km, bear left onto Sigalet Lake Forest Service Road. After 0.6 km up Sigalet FSR, turn right into the access of Haggkvist Lake, and drive 0.4 km of rough road into Haggkvist Lake Recreation Site.

name: Skunk Lake
driving_directions: Travel ~11kms S(SW) from Mackenzie and turn right on to the Causeway (then turn left). After crossing the bridge over Williston Lake keep to the right and merge with the Finlay North FSR at ~20km.  At ~62.5km take the Finlay-Nation FSR until you reach the Thutade and turn right. The site is located an additional 5kms.

name: Edwin Lakes
driving_directions: From Lavington, travel Aberdeen FSR to 10.75km mile marker, and turn left onto Haddo FSR. After 1.7km on Haddo FSR, keep left onto Edwin FSR. Edwin Lake is another 3.7km to the lake.

name: Skyline Lake
driving_directions: From Clearwater on Yellowhead Hwy 5, proceed 25 km east and turn south onto Vavenby Bridge Rd. After 1.5km, turn left to stay on this road.  Continue onto Birch Island/Lost Creek Rd., then continue straight onto Road 2/Adams Lake Rd and turn left at 13.5 km. The 1 km access road into site is very rough.

name: Pinkut Lake
driving_directions: Near Burns Lake, head north on the Babine Road for 19.5 km, until you reach the Augier FSR.  Cross the Augier road and follow the small road to the Pinkut Lake site (~500 Meters)

name: Little Slocan
driving_directions: The most popular access to Little Slocan Lakes campsite is from Passmore along Highway 6.  As you drive through Passmmore heading north turn left off of the highway onto Passmore Upper Road.  Cross the river and follow the road for 3.7 km.  Turn left onto the Little Slocan Forest Service Rd..  Stay on the main road for approx 21 km to the recreation site on your right.

name: Monashee-Kettle
driving_directions: Turn North off HWY 6 onto Keefer Forest Service Road. Drive 1.6 km to the Rec Site along a good road.

name: Weston Bay
driving_directions: Travel north of Mackenzie on the Parsnip West FSR. The site is located at km 74 - turn left and follow this road for approx. 1.5 km into the site.

name: Division Lake
driving_directions: Near Burns Lake, from Hwy 16 head north at Babine Lake Road for 17.3 kms.  Site is on the right hand side and is marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Stony Lake North
driving_directions: From Highway 97, turn onto the Naver Creek (700) Road at Dunkley Mill. Follow this road for approximately 58km and turn left onto the Willow-Stony Road. Follow this road and keep to the right when you reach a junction. Proceed along this road and this will be the second rec site you reach along the right side of the road.

name: Poplar Lake
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 near Houston, turn onto Morice River FSR, proceed about 40km down Morice River FSR (driving past Aspen and Owen Lake Recreation Sites amongst others), the FSR turns to Morice Owen, then you turn right onto Morice Nadina FSR at about 60km, proceed on Morice Nadina FSR for about 15km. Then turn right on MOrice Tahtsa road and proceed acorss Nadina River, then take the first right up Tahtsa FSR for about 2km, then turn left at the major junction marked with a road sign, proceed on this road for about 4km, then turn right down towards the lake and the site access road will be on your right marked with a 3 blade sign.

name: Francois West
driving_directions: From Hwy 16 in Burns Lake, take Hwy 35 south and turn west onto Colleymount Rd. From Northbank ferry terminal, head west ~55 km along Colleymount Road, take a left at the Colleymount/Owen East Rd junction onto Oots-Nadina FSR. Follow Ootsa-Nadina FSR south for 4 km around west point of lake, turn left onto the access road to access the site.

name: Warm Bay
driving_directions: Approx. 24km south of Atlin on Warm Bay Road.   Warm Springs (private) at 25km, and Grotto Recreation Site at ~27km.

name: Tsikwustum Creek North
driving_directions: North Adams Lake area, east side, km 7.5.

name: Aileen Lake
driving_directions: Accessed easiest through Lavington off Learmouth Road. Drive up Aberdeen Forest Service Road to mile marker 20. At 20.6 km, set odometer to 0 and take unmarked road to the right. At 1.4km on the odometer, take sharp turn right. Through this last cutblock there are water bars, and large water puddles in the remaining 800m into the lake. Aileen Lake is at 2.7km on the odometer.

name: Mohr Creek
driving_directions: This is a site along the Kettle River main road. It is situated near the 79.5 km board on the Kettle FSR.

name: Buckhorn Lake
driving_directions: Travel 17kms south of Prince George.  Turn left on to the Willow Cale FSR (112.5km). Turn right at 121km (T junction) and the site is located at km 123.

name: Camp Creek Trails
driving_directions: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 11 km.  Turn east and continue for 2.5 km to the parking area and trailhead, staying left.

name: Monica Meadows Site
driving_directions: From Kaslo: Driving time= 1.5 hrs, 2wd high clearance vehicle required. From Kaslo head North on hwy 31N towards Lardeau/Duncan Lake. Turn right on Argenta Rd (35km from Kaslo), and set your odometer to 0. Cross a bridge and reach a junction at 2.3 km, proceed straight. At 12 km turn right(North-East) and ascend onto Duncan-Glacier Creek FSR. At 22.5 reach a fork and proceed straight(east). At 36 km, immediately after a bridge, reach a junction and turn left (northwest. At 37.7 km fork right on Monica road. Expect deep water bars for the rest of the way. At 43 km reach the trailhead and parking pullout.

name: Lower Nation Falls
driving_directions: From Mackenzie, travel south to the Causeway Road. Turn left at the T junction just off the highway and after crossing the bridge, keep right and continue along the Finlay North FSR. At 62.5 km turn left onto the Finlay Nation FSR. The entrance to the site is located on the right side of the road about 12km from the turnoff.

name: Pinnacle Lake Trail Head
driving_directions: Travel time: +/- 2hrs. From Vernon take Hwy 6 past Lumby for 66 km. Turn left 1.5 km past Goldpanner Cafe onto South Fork Forest Service Road. Drive past the Pinnacles Hiking Area sign post. Continue for another 22.5 km following the signs and park in the log landing area.

name: Trout Camp
driving_directions: Traveling North from Nakusp BC on Hwy 23 , turn onto Hwy 31 heading East to Trout Lake BC . Travel past Trout Lake BC till you are the east end of the lake at Gerrard BC . At Gerrard BC  head up the Southeast side of the lake on West Trout Road FSR +/- 1.142 km . and there will be a access point to the lake .

name: Paulson Cross-Country
driving_directions: The Paulson Cross Country Ski Trails are situated 30 km west of Castlegar, along Highway #3, adjacent to Nancy Greene Provincial Park.

name: RIPPLE / LIGHTNING CABINS
driving_directions: From Salmo take Highways #6 and #3 southeast for 37 km to Stayleep pass at Bridal Lake. Park in the plowed area on the left side of the highway. From the junction of Highways #3 and #3A north of Creston take highway #3 northwest for 42.5 km to the pass at Bridal Lake. Park in the plowed area on the north side of the highway. From the parking area, cross the highway towards the south. The gravel road accessing the cabin begins immediately to the right of the Highway's maintenance yard. Take this road 3.2 km to the top of the ridge where it levels off and before it drops into the next valley. Look for the trail into the cabins on the right at this point. The old cabin lies about 200 metres from the access road, and the new cabin about 100 metres further. high clearance 2WD required.

name: Harris Lake
driving_directions: From Nakusp head north on Highway 23 towards the Galena Bay Ferry for 40 km. You will see a single 4x4 post stating Harris Lake on your right at the turn off. The road is easy to miss but it is about 5 minutes past Halcyon Hotsprings. Follow down this road for a couple hundred meters until you reach the recreation site sign and pull out.

name: CANTY LAKE TRAIL (Parking lot)
driving_directions: Travel north (NW) of Mackenzie via the Parsnip West FSR, and turn right at approx. km 89.5. Access to this trail head is located ~3kms off the main FSR.

name: Oliver (Johny Connors) Lake
driving_directions: From the community of Crawford Bay, head south for 200 meters on Highway3A, and then turn left on Oliver Road just past the Gray Creek store. Follow this road for 300 meters and then turn right, crossing Gray Creek. Follow Anderson road, for 1.3 km, turning left at the junction. Follow the main Gray Creek road 15.0 km to the campsite.

name: Vista Pass Trail Head
driving_directions: Travel time: +/- 2hrs. From Vernon take Hwy 6 past Lumby for 66 km. Turn left 1.5 km past Goldpanner Cafe onto South Fork Forest Service Road. Drive past the Pinnacles Hiking Area sign post and follow the Vista Pass sign posts for at least 21.5 km until you reach the trailhead. The road is passable for vehicles with good clearance.

name: Monashee Lake Trail Head
driving_directions: Travel time: +/- 2hrs. from Vernon take Hwy 6 past Lumby for 66 km. Turn left 1.5 km past Goldpanner Cafe onto South Fork Forest Service Road. Drive past the Pinnacles Hiking Area sign post for about 24 km following Monashee Creek to reach the trailhead following the Monashee Lake signs. The road is passable for cars with good clearance.

name: Teapot Mountain
driving_directions: Travel 50 Km north of Prince George on Hwy 97 past Summit Lake. From Highway 97 turn left on to Talus Road. Continue driving and then take a right on to the Caine Creek Forest Road. Follow the road to the parking lot.

name: Idaho Peak
driving_directions: ROAD IS WAASHED OUT AT 1.5KM AND 2KM AND IS NOT PASSIBLE BY VEHICLE.  At the junction of Hwy 6 and 31A in New Denver, turn east onto Hwy 31A and follow the signs to Sandon. In Sandon, cross the bridge and continue through the centre of town, stopping to pick up drinking water and anything else you may need for the trip. At the end of the street, stop and read the "Idaho Peak Information Sign". This sign has important road information. The first 2 km of the road is wide, not too steep and well maintained by the mining companies. After this, the road narrows considerably, as it switch backs up the mountain. As you enter Wild Goose Basin, you will find a pleasant picnic site on the edge of the meadow. From here, the rest of the road is clearly visible, as it switch backs up to the 2 parking areas. The most heavily used parking area is on the ridge between Idaho Peak and Selkirk Peak. The Alamo parking area is less crowded. Perfect! Park here to avoid the crowds around the ridge parking lot or protect your vehicle's paint job from the nicks and scratches acquired in crowded parking lots.

name: Panther Lake
driving_directions: From the junction of Highway 3B and 3/6 in Salmo, travel south on Highway 6 towards Creston for 7.2 km. Turn left onto "Airport Road", opposite the Kootenay Stone Centre. Travel 2.3 km north, crossing over the Sheep Creek bridge. Turn right onto "Sheep Creek Road". This road is paved for the first half kilometre, then turns into good 2 wheel drive gravel road. There are many roads branching off the Sheep Creek Road, choose the most travelled route that follows along the valley bottom, on the left side of the creek. (Most junctions will have a sign directing you up the Sheep Creek Road). Stay left at 6.5 km. Left again at Sheep-Waldie FSR (11 km). Left at 14 km and start climbing away from creek, 4x4 from here on. Turn right at bridge (15km) and take the next right in ~1 km at small logging spur rd. Trailhead begins at the end of the logging block.

name: Twin Lakes Trail Head
driving_directions: Travel time: +/- 2hrs. From Vernon take Hwy 6 past Lumby for about 53 km past the Sugar Lake turn-off and turn left on North Fork Road. Go past the school and community hall then at about 6.5 km make a sharp left onto the North Fork Forest Service Road. Follow it for 14 km, following the signs as it switchbacks uphill until you reach the parking lot. This road is only passable for cars with good clearance.

name: Ross-White Lady Lake
driving_directions: From the ferry terminal at Balfour, travel west on highway #3A for 2.7 km to Beggs Road on the right. Keep to the left, and follow Beggs road for 0.8 km to a fork in the road. Stay left and drive 0.3 km to Redfish Forest service road on the left (cross over Laird Creek). Follow Redfish forest service road (keep right at the junction with the Redfish Research Area) for 10.3 km to a bridge. Drive across the bridge and drive the remaining 1.0 km to a road that leads to the right. The bridge across this road is damaged, so you will need to walk the remaining portion of the road to the trailhead. The trail begins on an old skid trail to the north-west.

name: Ripple (Silver) Lake
driving_directions: From 100 Mile House, travel south on Hwy 97 and turn left (east) onto Hwy 24.  Travel about 60 km east on Hwy 24 and turn left onto the Wavey Lake Road. Travel about 10.6 km up the Wavey Lake Road to Ripple Lake.

name: Buhl Creek
driving_directions: Approximately 5kms north of the community of Canal Flats take the Findlay Creek FS Road west to the 8 km marker.  Turn south on to the Skookumchuck FS Road , staying right at the 17 km mark .  Follow the main Skookumchuck FS road to the Buhl Creek turnoff at 44.8km.  Staying left here will bring you to the site located on the right side of the road.

name: Tony Lake
driving_directions:
For up to date road information call 604 485 3132
From Powell River head south on Highway 101 to Lang Bay. Turn left onto Dixon Road and drive to the junction with Goat Lake Main, turn left on Goat Lake Main.  Follow the one-way directions and watch for logging traffic. Double back at the resumption of two-way traffic for about 300 meters and turn left onto the Stillwater Main. Turn left again on the minor road in about 1km. Follow this road to the end at Tony Lake.

name: Needa Lake
driving_directions: From 100 Mile House, travel about 8 km south on Hwy 97 and turn left/east onto Hwy 24. Travel 38.5 km east along Hwy 24 and turn left/north onto Judson Road.  Travel 2.4 km and keep straight/right (rejoin the pavement at Shertenlib Road). Go another 0.7 km and turn left/go straight, turning onto Judson Road.  Travel 2.7 km and turn right onto the Windy Mountain Forest Service Road.  Travel 11.7 km and turn right/east onto the access road into the recreation site. Travel 1.0 km to the Needa Lake Recreation Site.

name: Canuck Creek Site
driving_directions: From Yahk, head East on Highway #3, cross a bridge and take the Yahk-Meadow Creek Road to the right. Continue on this road for 6.5km to the recreation site on the right. The road is suitable for 2wd vehicles. This is an active logging road, so turn your lights on and drive carefully.

name: Abbott Creek
driving_directions:
From Likely follow the Cariboo River Road, turn Right up the hill on Spanish Lake Road (1300rd), and follow this for approximately 17km. Turn right and follow this road till the end.

The last hill before the site is long and steep, but easily done by larger units.

name: Labour Day Lake
driving_directions:
From Port Alberni, take Highway 4 east toward Parksville.  Just before the Alberni Summit brake check turn right onto the Cameron Connector. Once through the gate reset your odometer. At 2.6km turn left onto Cameron River Main. At 8.3 cross the bridge and stay left. At 10.1 take a right at the fork. Again at 10.5 stay right. At 12.8 drive straight. At 15.4 turn left at junction. Take the left fork at 21.7 (through red gate). At 24.1 park in a large pullout on the right. The trail begins about 50m up the road on the right hand side. 

Access to Labour Day Lake Recreation Site is via privately managed roads. For information on road access and gate closures please check the following website before you travel: https://www.mosaicforests.com/access

name: BIG LAKE / Delgi Chosh
driving_directions: From Williams Lake, follow Hwy 20 for approximately 90 km to "Lee's Corner" at Hanceville. Turn left/south onto Big Creek Road (700 Road). Follow Big Creek Road (700 Road) about 5 km and turn right onto Taseko Road, following signage to Stone (Yunesit'in) and Nemaiah Valley. Eventually this road joins the 900 Road at about the 913 km marker.  The Big Lake Recreation Site is located at about 71 km on the 900 / Taseko Road.

name: Greenlee Lake
driving_directions: From 100 Mile House travel north on Hwy 97 for approximately 2 km and turn right/east onto the Canim-Hendrix Lake Road. Travel 21 km to Forest Grove and turn right/east, remaining on the Canim-Hendrix Lake Road, and continue another 24 km.  Turn left onto the Eagle Creek Road.
